summary.oneLiner: G. G. Dandekar Properties Limited is a small Pune-based commercial real-estate company operating in a single vertical - leasing of commercial property - with owned office properties in Pune and Nagpur generating steady lease rental income in the form of license fees.
summary.business: The Company is engaged in the real estate leasing business and, during FY 2025-26, continued to operate in only one vertical: commercial real estate - leasing of commercial property. It owns properties in Pune and Nagpur which are let out to occupiers and generate lease rental income in the form of license fees. Alongside leasing, the Company provides allied services to occupants such as upkeep and maintenance of the property, security and housekeeping, for which it charges maintenance fees separately at monthly intervals.

currentContext.strengths: Owned, unchanged commercial property portfolio in Pune and Nagpur generating steady, recurring lease rental income in the form of license fees|Located in Maharashtra, the state that attracted the highest FDI inflows in India during FY 2025-26, with Pune commercial real estate benefiting from infrastructure development, improving connectivity and industrial expansion|Broad tenant base rather than single-customer dependence: the Company states it is not reliant on any one customer, though revenue from each of six customers exceeds ten percent of revenue from operations|Post year-end service agreement with Bootstart Spaces and Hospitality Private Limited to professionally manage and operate the owned office spaces, which the Board believes will maximize occupancy and improve service standards|Very lean cost base - total workforce of 3 employees as on 31 March 2026, commensurate with the scale of operations
currentContext.strategies: Remain a single-vertical commercial real-estate leasing company: the Company continues to operate in only one vertical, commercial real estate - leasing of commercial property, from the same number of owned properties in Pune and Nagpur.|Strengthen the management of its commercial real estate assets and enhance the quality of services provided to occupants through a Service Agreement with Bootstart Spaces and Hospitality Private Limited for the management and operation of the Company's owned office spaces, which the Board expects will maximize occupancy, run the office spaces efficiently, raise customer service standards and ensure better utilization of assets.|Continue efforts of efficient property management, maintaining quality infrastructure and enhancing customer experience.|Board-stated mitigation agenda for the risks it monitors: portfolio diversification, active tenant management, prudent leverage levels, cost control, succession planning and technology-driven productivity improvements.|Manage the holding in associate Navasasyam Dandekar Private Limited actively: the Board declined the NDPL rights issue of 15 July 2025, had its CCPS holding converted into equity shares, and tendered shares into NDPL's buy-back offer, reducing the Company's stake from 49% to 33.31% while NDPL remains an associate.
currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no capex or expansion project. The Company states that during the year under review it continued to have the same number of properties owned by it, with both properties, in Pune and Nagpur, generating steady lease rental income in the form of license fees, and that it continues to operate in only one vertical - commercial real estate leasing. The only forward-looking asset-related development is organisational rather than capital: after the end of the financial year the Company entered into a Service Agreement with Bootstart Spaces and Hospitality Private Limited (a related party with effect from 2 June 2026) for the management and operation of the office spaces owned by the Company, which the Board expects will maximize occupancy and ensure better utilization of the Company's existing assets. There is no new property acquisition, construction, commissioning or ramp-up narrative in the routed text.
currentContext.mdna: Outlook stated as positive on expansion of Global Capability Centres and multinational corporations, sustained demand for professionally managed office spaces and increasing preference for flexible and managed workspaces.|Stable demand from IT, engineering, consulting, healthcare, education and financial services sectors is expected to drive further growth.|Infrastructure development in Pune seems to be improving the commercial attractiveness of the city.|Maharashtra attracted the highest Foreign Direct Investment inflows in India during FY 2025-26; this investment climate together with rising commercial activity in and around Pune has driven stronger demand for commercial real estate.|As employers with larger workforces increasingly prefer office-based operations over remote work, demand for flexible leasing solutions such as co-working spaces and managed offices has grown substantially, further supported by innovative office concepts, business-friendly initiatives and high-quality tenant amenities.|Occupiers increasingly seek professionally managed workspaces providing integrated facilities and value-added services, with leasing activity healthy across major cities.|Pune's real estate growth is driven by IT, education, automobile and manufacturing sectors, and investments valued at more than Rs. 650 Bn are expected to be infused over eight years for metro rail links, a new airport terminal and a ring road.

risks.risk: Concentration risk - revenue from a limited number of properties and locations
risks.note: Management flags that a significant portion of the Company's revenue is derived from a limited number of properties and geographic locations, which may increase vulnerability to localized market downturns, tenant defaults or regulatory changes. The whole business sits in one operating segment, 'Renting / Leasing of Immovable Properties', in a single geographical location - the state of Maharashtra - with only two owned properties, in Pune and Nagpur.

risks.risk: Tenant concentration - a handful of customers carry the rent roll
risks.note: The segment note states the Company is not reliant on any one customer, but that revenue contributed by each of its six customers exceeds ten percent of revenue from operations. Losing or re-pricing any one of those leases moves a disproportionate share of income.

Management flags that volatility in interest rates and changes in financing conditions could increase debt servicing costs and impact cash flow and profitability. The financial-instruments note adds that the Company's borrowing is linked to the repo rate and is therefore floating-rate, so the Company is currently exposed to interest-rate risk. The MD&A threats list separately notes that rising interest rates have a firm impact on real estate markets and reduce customer demand.

risks.risk: Financial performance risk - elevated fixed costs and finance expenses against a small rent base
risks.note: Management flags that elevated fixed costs and finance expenses may compress margins or produce low or negative returns on certain investments, particularly during periods of subdued rental growth. The Company reported a loss before exceptional items and tax in both FY 2025-26 and the prior year.

risks.risk: Key management personnel and human capital dependency
risks.note: Management flags that the Company's relatively flat organizational structure and lean team create dependency on a small number of key individuals, and that changes in KMP or shifts in workforce requirements driven by technology adoption such as AI may affect operational continuity and execution. Total workforce was 3 employees as on 31 March 2026.

Management flags that adverse geopolitical developments or global economic headwinds could weaken investor confidence and slow demand for commercial real estate, negatively affecting leasing activity and asset valuations. The MD&A threats list adds political uncertainty - changes in leadership affecting the taxation system linked to real estate, and war between countries - and economy/affordability, where a weaker economy reduces potential customers' affordability.

risks.risk: Property title not recorded in the Company's name in Property Tax records
risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to Note 58(ix) on title deeds of certain immovable properties: the properties are owned by and in the possession of the Company and titled in its name, but the Company's name is yet to be incorporated in the Property Tax records. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.

risks.risk: Statutory dues in arrears - unpaid provident fund and pension scheme contributions
risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to Note 28.3 on unpaid Employee's Contribution to the Provident Fund and Employer's Contribution towards the Employee's Pension Scheme for the months from September 2025 to March 2026, attributed to technical issues encountered while remitting the amounts electronically. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.

The MD&A threats list names natural disasters as adversely affecting the real estate industry, and cites regulatory changes and compliance requirements alongside economic affordability as threats to the sector.
